description: worldsteel collects data directly from steel producers in its global membership and publishes steel production, use and trade statistics. Coverage: global, by country and company; the free World Steel in Figures 2026 report covers world crude steel production from 1950 to 2025, the top 50 steel-producing companies, production by process, monthly production 2022 to 2025, apparent and true steel use per capita, pig iron, direct reduced iron, iron ore and ferrous scrap, world steel trade from 1975, indirect trade in steel and the industry's sustainability indicators; the paid subscriptions give monthly iron and crude steel production from the 70 countries that report monthly, and the Steel Statistical Yearbook 2025 with data from 2015 to 2024. Format and access: World Steel in Figures as a web report and a free PDF; the subscriptions on the worldsteel data platform give Excel downloads and a PDF after login, with monthly figures uploaded between the 22nd and 25th of the following month; employees of member companies have free access through the extranet. Licence: subscription data are worldsteel copyright and may be used internally but not shared with third parties; terms for the free report were not read. Caveats: the paid tiers cost 1,590 euros a year for monthly data plus the yearbook and 730 euros for the yearbook alone; the Steel Data Viewer needs a login. Simulation uses: steel production and trade baselines for supply chain and capacity planning studies of construction materials and transport equipment. Related records: the GCCA cement database (data-gcca-gnr-cement-co2-energy-database) is the matching source for cement.
